trello.name: Implement queue depth alerts for all worker fleets
trello.desc: Create monitoring and alerting on worker queue depth to eliminate blind spot identified during outage. Kofi owns. Scope: all worker fleets, not just payments, with same thresholds. Warning threshold at 1,000 jobs, page threshold at 5,000 jobs. Steps: 1) Identify queue depth metric source for each worker fleet. 2) Create alert rules with warning at 1,000 and page at 5,000. 3) Test alerts in staging by simulating queue growth. 4) Document alert runbook link. Acceptance criteria: Alerts fire in test, notification routes to on-call, dashboard shows queue depth per fleet, no queue depth alert gaps for payment workers.

trello.name: Fix payment worker retry logic and dead-letter queue
trello.desc: Remediate retry storm in payment_worker.py _process_with_retry that caused self-DDoS during card processor 503s. Marta owns. Steps: 1) Replace immediate retries with exponential backoff with jitter. 2) Cap retries to five attempts. 3) Change failure handling: on fifth failure, move job to dead-letter queue at back instead of re-enqueueing at front of main queue. 4) Add unit/integration tests simulating processor 503 responses to verify backoff, jitter, cap, and dead-letter routing. Acceptance criteria: Code review passes, tests cover 503 storm scenario, no front-of-queue re-enqueue, dead-letter queue receives failed jobs, load test shows no retry amplification.

trello.name: Increase DB connection pool and isolate worker/API pools
trello.desc: Prevent connection pool exhaustion coupling workers and API. Kofi owns. Steps: 1) Bump DB connection pool from default 20 to 100 as immediate mitigation. 2) Split configuration so worker fleet and API service use separate connection pools instead of shared pool. 3) Update same config file for both changes. 4) Validate pool sizes in staging under load. Acceptance criteria: Config shows worker pool and API pool separate, max connections >=100 per pool, load test with worker spike does not exhaust API connections, monitoring confirms pool utilization.

trello.name: Update payment incident runbook
trello.desc: Refresh payment incident runbook to remove stale references and document improvised procedures. Assign to Priya. Steps: 1) Replace old Kibana links with current logging/links active since March decommission. 2) Document queue drain procedure Kofi improvised on Tuesday. 3) Verify escalation phone numbers are current; remove numbers for departed staff. 4) Publish updated runbook and notify on-call. Acceptance criteria: Runbook links resolve, queue drain procedure is step-by-step, escalation contacts verified current, Priya confirms completion.

trello.name: Automate status page updates on checkout error rate
trello.desc: Reduce manual status page delay. Marta owns. Automate status page to flip to 'investigating' when checkout error rate alert fires, using template message. Steps: 1) Use status provider API to create automation webhook. 2) Wire automation to checkout error rate alert. 3) Provide template investigating message. 4) Test automation in staging. Acceptance criteria: Simulated checkout error rate alert triggers status page update automatically within 1 minute, message matches template, manual steps no longer required for initial incident.

trello.name: Draft payment processor failover game day plan
trello.desc: Validate secondary payment processor failover capability that was never exercised. Kofi leads. Steps: 1) Draft controlled chaos test plan for payment processor failover in staging first, then production during low-traffic window. 2) Include success criteria, rollback plan, communication plan, and risk assessment. 3) Submit plan for review in two weeks. 4) No execution until plan is reviewed and approved. Acceptance criteria: Written plan exists covering staging and production test steps, rollback procedures documented, review meeting scheduled, execution blocked pending approval.

trello.name: Upgrade Redis from 6.0 to 7.2
trello.desc: Address EOL Redis 6.0 security risk. Kofi owns. Steps: 1) Schedule change window with infra calendar, not casual Friday deploy. 2) Review config rename changes and persistence defaults changes between 6.0 and 7.2. 3) Perform upgrade in staging, validate persistence and config. 4) Execute production upgrade in scheduled window with rollback plan. Acceptance criteria: Production Redis running 7.2, config migrated, persistence defaults verified, security patches active, post-upgrade health checks pass.
